protocol.board: one grime-market plaza, 20x20 cells of 2:1 dimetric 64x32 tiles, authored once and shared

framings.note: every framing is a whole-number scale; treatment B is never resampled

controls: shared board model: floor plan, prop manifest, projection, cameras, unit roster
shared prop geometry: both treatments fill the identical polygons
shared palette: a machine-checked 51-colour set (palette.test.ts asserts both treatments stay inside it)
shared unit layer: the same placeholder sprites composited by the same code over both boards

valueSaturationBudget.note: measured off the treatment B buffer with the unit layer composited
valueSaturationBudget.reading: the board runs far quieter than 70/25/5 on purpose - canon says playable map regions keep quieter contrast so units own the darkest contours and brightest points. The identity band here lives almost entirely on stall canopies and crates. At 1280x720 with 34 small units the roster cannot move the ratio; at a tighter combat aperture the identity share rises.

treatmentA.rasterizer: browser (Image + drawImage); sharp/resvg would be the build-time equivalent, deliberately not added as a dependency

treatmentB.note: software rasterizer in plain TS, no canvas, no dependency; a production pipeline would bake this to a PNG once

authoringEffort.unitsOfMeasure: this is an agent session, so effort is reported as authored artifacts and build-inspect rounds, not human hours

files: borrowed-medic-48.ts 314 (copied lane art, not authored here)
sharedInfrastructure.amortises: across every future map, both treatments

perBoardAuthoring.propShapeBuilders: 11 kinds, ~230 lines in prop-geometry.ts - reusable across maps in the same district vocabulary
perBoardAuthoring.treatmentASurfaceWork: 0 - the register is entirely the two-pass ink and the flat fills, which are board-independent
perBoardAuthoring.treatmentBGeneratedPasses: ~130 lines of material detail (wood/steel/rust/concrete/plum/canvas/grate) - board-independent, reused by every map

treatmentBAuthoredStamps.reusable: only inside the same district vocabulary - a foundry or a clinic needs its own motifs

buildInspectRounds.round1: first full build of both treatments, board at 640x360 with 32x16 tiles
buildInspectRounds.round2: scale correction - a 48x64 hero read four tiles tall, so the board was rebuilt at 1280x720 with 64x32 tiles
buildInspectRounds.round3: dressing pass - apron rings, awning valances, southern props, calmer floor clusters, unit formations moved onto open ground
buildInspectRounds.note: rounds 1 and 3 were cheap because geometry is shared; round 2 was cheap for the same reason - every prop rescaled from one projection change

layerContribution.note: how many of the 921,600 board pixels each layer of treatment B is responsible for
layerContribution.geometryOnly: the flat baseline - every pixel, no surface

map2SameDistrict.description: a second grime-market board - different plan, same vocabulary
map2SameDistrict.treatmentA: floor plan + prop manifest only, ~80 lines. Prop shapes and the ink register carry over unchanged.
map2SameDistrict.treatmentB: the same ~80 lines. Generated passes carry over unchanged; the five stamps carry over because the motifs still fit.
map2SameDistrict.verdict: the two treatments cost the same for map 2. Density is free the second time only because the district did not change.

map3DifferentDistrict.description: a foundry, a clinic block, a transit yard - new material vocabulary
map3DifferentDistrict.treatmentA: ~80 lines of plan/manifest plus ~5 new prop-shape builders (~110 lines) plus optionally a district palette (~20 lines). The register still needs no per-map work.
map3DifferentDistrict.treatmentB: everything treatment A needs, PLUS a fresh authored stamp set. The existing 913 cells are market wares; a foundry needs crucibles, slag, tool racks, cable drums. At the density this board achieved that is another ~900 authored cells minimum, and this board is nowhere near MST density.
map3DifferentDistrict.verdict: treatment A's marginal cost per map is flat. Treatment B's marginal cost per map has a hand-authored term that does not amortise, and that term is the only part of B that produces objects rather than texture.

costToActuallyReachMSTDensity.estimatedRequiredShare: 0.15 - 0.25 of the board carrying authored motif rather than generated surface
costToActuallyReachMSTDensity.impliedMultiplier: 27x - 45x more authored cells for THIS board
costToActuallyReachMSTDensity.impliedStampCount: roughly 135 - 225 stamps at the current 180-cells-each average, versus the 5 authored here
costToActuallyReachMSTDensity.perMap: and that number is per map, for every map that is not a re-dress of the same district

toolboxUsed: browser SVG rasterization for treatment A
a hand-written software rasterizer for treatment B (pixel-canvas.ts)
ImageMagick for montaging filmstrips and layer studies
